albuild capabilities - Every command, option, exit code and refusal reason, as JSON for an agent.

A person finds a command through --help, one screen at a time. An agent has to choose
before it acts, and sixty help screens is not a plan.

This is the same catalogue the help is built from, so the two cannot drift, plus the
exit codes, the shape of the result envelope, and the stable reasons a probe gives when
it refuses. Branch on the codes; show the sentences to a person.

Usage: albuild capabilities [--json]
Positional arguments: none

Options: none of its own — see the global options below.

Examples:
  albuild capabilities --json

Global options:
  --output <mode>     text (humans, default) | json (one envelope) | ndjson (event stream).
  --json              Alias for --output json.
  --no-color          Disable ANSI colors (also honours NO_COLOR / CI / non-TTY).
  --verbose, -v       Stream diagnostics/logs to stderr.
  --dry-run           Validate + show the plan; no side effects.
  --yes, -y           Confirm a destructive command without prompting.
  --non-interactive   Never prompt. Without --yes a destructive command fails
                      NEEDS_CONFIRMATION instead of hanging or aborting.
                      Implied when stdin is not a terminal (agents, CI).
  --no-wait           Start the async job and return its jobId at once; don't wait. exit 0 = ACCEPTED,
                      not succeeded — poll 'albuild job get <id>'. (aliases --async/--detach; env ALBUILD_NO_WAIT=1; MCP only.)
  --server <name|url> Target MCP server. Default: ALBUILD_SERVER, then the configured default
                      profile, then the local direct backend (PowerShell, no MCP).
  --backend <b>       Local backend: direct (default) or mcp (a local stdio MCP server).
  --container <name>  Target container.
  --project <path>    App folder (app.json).
  --workspace <path>  Repo root (albuild.json).
  --timeout <sec>     Cap long operations.
  --help, -h          Show this help. Never runs the command.
  --commands    
[truncated]

  [destructive] Needs --yes when stdin is not a terminal.

On a build server this one directory decides how much can be cached and how many
containers fit: a BC container restores its database into its writable layer, and a

albuild probe call - Run one AL procedure locally with the arguments you give it (no container).

Answers 'what does this actually return for these inputs' in milliseconds: your AL is
compiled by Microsoft's own compiler and the result runs against ALbuild's runtime
surface. No container, no publish, no test app. This is a REASONING tool:
it tells you about a function, it does not tell you a release is good — there is no service
tier behind it, so tables start EMPTY, Commit does nothing (an error does not roll back), and anything that cannot be done
faithfully fails loudly instead of returning a plausible value.

Usage: albuild probe call --target '"<object>"::<procedure>' [--args <json>] [--set <json>] [--trace]
Positional arguments: [target]

Options:
  --target <t>                 '"<object>"::<procedure>', e.g. '"bdev.BNK Bank Formatter"::FormatIBAN'. Prefix with Table/Codeunit to disambiguate.
  --args <json>                JSON array of arguments, positional, converted to each parameter's declared AL type.
  --set <json|@file>           Seed the in-memory tables: {"Currency":[{"Code":"EUR"}]}, or @seed.json to read it from disk. Nothing else is in them.
  --project <dir>              The AL project - the folder holding app.json; a repo root is refused. Defaults to the working directory.
  --today <date>               Pin Today()/CurrentDateTime() so the probe is reproducible (default 2026-01-15).
  --work-date <date>           Pin WorkDate().
  --user <id>                  What UserId() returns (default 'PROBE').
  --company <name>             What CompanyName() returns (default 'CRONUS').
  --timeout <s>                How long the AL may run before the probe stops it, in seconds (default 30).
  --trace                      Report what the run DID, in order: every AL statement with its file and line - an if reports its condition, then the branch taken - and between them what the runtime was asked to do. Off by default; it costs a string per call into the runtime.
  --emit-test                  Emit the cas

albuild probe mutate - Mutation testing for AL: change the code a little, see whether the tests notice.

Mutation testing, for AL. Every small change to the source that the test suite does NOT
notice is a place where the code could be wrong and nothing would say so. Coverage tells
you a line ran; this tells you whether anything CHECKED it.

What makes it possible at all is the cost of a run. Mutation testing needs hundreds of
executions, and at a container apiece that is arithmetic, not tooling, ruling it out.
Here a mutant costs one compile plus the handful of tests that reach it - the runtime
records which AL procedures each test entered, so the rest of the suite is not run.

TWO NUMBERS, and reporting one of them would mislead: the score over everything judged,
and the score over what a test actually reaches. The gap between them is untested code.

A mutant that does not compile, or whose covering tests all hit a limit of this runtime,
produces NO verdict and is excluded from both. Counting those as killed would flatter
every suite it measured. Tests that cannot run here at all - a TestPage that invokes an
action, navigates or traps a page, or a report layout - are named BEFORE the score,
because they bound what it means. A TestPage that only opens a page on a record and
reads or sets its fields does run.

PROPOSED MUTANTS. The operators are syntactic; the gaps that matter are often not - a
rounding precision, a swapped field, a missing filter. --mutants runs a list of changes
somebody proposed (an agent that read the code, typically) instead of the generated
set. Each is checked before the baseline: its text must really stand on that line,
inside a procedure body of the app, outside test code. One that does not is refused
and named, never run - a proposal that missed by a line would answer another question.

Test code is never mutated, and the source on disk is restored whatever happens.

Usage: albuild probe mutate [<app-dir>] [--tests <dir>] [--include <substr,...>] [--operators <list>] [--mutants <file|->]
[truncated]

albuild probe batch - Run many probes from one JSON file in a single process.

The cost of a probe is the round trip, not the run. Checking twenty inputs against
one function should cost one invocation. The file is a JSON array of
{ "target": "…", "args": [ … ] } or { "code": "…", "vars": "…" } entries.
Exits non-zero if any probe in the batch failed.

With --verify --container <c> the batch becomes a DIFFERENTIAL CORPUS: every case is
answered twice, once here and once by a real Business Central, and every disagreement is
named. That is slow - each case publishes a test to the container - so it belongs in a
nightly build, not in the dev loop. It is also the only thing that keeps this runtime
honest as BC moves.

Usage: albuild probe batch <file.json> [--project <dir>]
Positional arguments: [file]

Options:
  --batch <file>               The JSON file of probes to run. May also be the first positional argument.
  --harness <path>             The differential harness --verify drives. Defaults to the copy shipped with the tool (env ALBUILD_PROBE_HARNESS also works).
  --set <json>                 Default table seed for every entry; an entry's own 'set' overrides it.
  --today <date>               Pin Today()/CurrentDateTime() (default 2026-01-15).
  --work-date <date>           Pin WorkDate().
  --user <id>                  What UserId() returns (default 'PROBE').
  --company <name>             What CompanyName() returns (default 'CRONUS').
  --timeout <s>                How long the AL may run per probe, in seconds (default 30).
  --trace                      Report what the run DID, in order: every AL statement with its file and line - an if reports its condition, then the branch taken - and between them what the runtime was asked to do. Off by default; it costs a string per call into the runtime.
  --seed-from-container <c>    Fill the in-memory tables with real rows read from this container, instead of inventing them.
  --seed-table <t>             Which table(s) to read, comma-separated. Required with --seed-f

albuild screenshot - Capture web client pages and reports from a container as PNGs.

Deterministic capture: sign in, navigate, wait, dismiss what covers the view, save a PNG,
and write a manifest naming the BC version, the company and the UI language the client
actually rendered in.

The browser runs where the container is REACHABLE, and the bytes come back — a container's
web client URL is often a NAT address that resolves only on the host. --out is a local path
on both backends, and no password or host path is ever passed by the caller.

Needs the capture browser: 'albuild setup --screenshots' (a few hundred MB, installed once).

Click-through demos, data entry and video are deliberately NOT here — they need a script,
and this takes a list of objects. Those stay in the bc-ui-capture skill.

Usage: albuild screenshot --container <c> [--pages <ids>] [--reports <ids>] [--out <dir>]
Positional arguments: [container]

Options:
  --pages <ids>                Comma-separated page object ids, e.g. 22,21.
  --reports <ids>              Comma-separated report object ids.
  --out <dir>                  Output directory ON THIS MACHINE. Default: ./screenshots.
  --company <name>             Company to open. Default: the container's default company.
  --language <culture>         UI culture, e.g. de-DE. Governs the browser language and which caption table is used — NOT the container's own default language.

  --full-page                  Capture the full scrollable content instead of the viewport.

  --filter <expr>              Record filter, so a card can target one record, e.g. "'No.' IS '10000'".
  --mode <m>                   View (default) or Edit. Create is not offered — it writes data.

Usage: albuild mcp status [options]
Positional arguments: none

Options: none of its own — see the global options below.

Global options:
  --output <mode>     text (humans, default) | json (one envelope) | ndjson (event stream).
  --json              Alias for --output json.
  --no-color          Disable ANSI colors (also honours NO_COLOR / CI / non-TTY).
  --verbose, -v       Stream diagnostics/logs to stderr.
  --dry-run           Validate + show the plan; no side effects.
  --yes, -y           Confirm a destructive command without prompting.
  --non-interactive   Never prompt. Without --yes a destructive command fails
                      NEEDS_CONFIRMATION instead of hanging or aborting.
                      Implied when stdin is not a terminal (agents, CI).
  --no-wait           Start the async job and return its jobId at once; don't wait. exit 0 = ACCEPTED,
                      not succeeded — poll 'albuild job get <id>'. (aliases --async/--detach; env ALBUILD_NO_WAIT=1; MCP only.)
  --server <name|url> Target MCP server. Default: ALBUILD_SERVER, then the configured default
                      profile, then the local direct backend (PowerShell, no MCP).
  --backend <b>       Local backend: direct (default) or mcp (a local stdio MCP server).
  --container <name>  Target container.
  --project <path>    App folder (app.json).
  --workspace <path>  Repo root (albuild.json).
  --timeout <sec>     Cap long operations.
  --help, -h          Show this help. Never runs the command.
  --commands          List every command path (one per line), for scripting.
  --version           Print the CLI version.
